chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Alto player Swindell
summary: Swindell, who lived next door to Charlie Parker, might have rivalled Parker had drugs not ruined him; he died after moving to the West Coast.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But apart from these guys -- I mean the other older musicians used to come there too, didn't they?

Yeah. Yeah, we had a boy there -- his wife is living in New York now. She was a very good musician. Name's Swindell, an alto player. If he hadn't of died, if he hadn't got on that stuff, I think he'd have been close to Charlie Parker. He used to come down there all the time. I'd say, go on, Swindell. Loved to hear him play.
Charlie lived right upstairs in the hotel next to it.
What was his first name? You don't know?

Oh, what was the name? Was it George? We all called him Swindell. His last name was (Unintelligible) Swindell, and his wife, when he got on that thing and he kind of went out of the picture, and then there was a group that came from California, and they wanted an alto player. He started straightening up then. And they'd taken him out to the West Coast. I said, well, good thing I couldn't get to him first, because stay out there because you'll make it out there. And he met this girl. She was going to college. And she was a very good musician. And he married her.
When they came back to New York, he died. I don't know whether it was pneumonia or what, TB or something like that, but he was a good alto player. Very fine alto player.
